test_groups.name: unresolved_drop_keeps_callee_priority_without_inspecting_its_argument
test_groups.expectation: drop(0), drop(q) and drop(not q) fail common name / finite unknown_name at exactly the callee span with identical conditional name hints. Unresolved missing(not q) keeps its old unhinted callee diagnostic. Unicode/CRLF source prefix does not change byte-span semantics.

test_groups.name: user_helpers_and_local_categories_do_not_acquire_rust_name_privileges
test_groups.expectation: User drop(Bit)->Unit stays Unitary and native closed execution returns 1. User drop(Q<Bit>)->Unit via explicit discard stays Observe and also returns 1. A quantum argument to the classical helper remains an argument type error; a runtime local drop remains a local-category error; an ordinary owner-transferring clone cannot permit the input owner to be used again. Those refusals gain no unresolved-name privilege or hint.

test_groups.name: ordinary_loss_remains_permitted_but_nested_zero_width_owners_cannot_disappear
test_groups.expectation: The same unused-parameter, wildcard, expression-statement, new-local-leak and live-shadow cases accept for (Bit,(Unit,Bit)) but reject for (Bit,(Unit,Q<Unit>)) at their original owner/pattern/expression spans with ownership category and preserved prefixes. Q<Unit> has zero wires but remains owned.

test_groups.name: reset_returns_an_owner_and_linear_shadowing_can_return_the_replacement
test_groups.expectation: reset(q); () remains an expression-statement ownership loss. Returning reset(q), and let q=h(q); q after consuming the previous binding, stay valid. A one-qubit H then reset then Z-readout has deterministic zero outcome and retains Observe versus Unitary inferred helper effects.

independent_execution_expectations: Pure ordinary drop returns explicitly authored Bit 1.
Explicit observing user drop consumes an initialized qubit through discard; subsequent ordinary Bit 1 is unchanged.
H prepares |+>; reset returns |0> as a fresh owner; observing it reads 0 with probability 1.
